name: Stratum Logistics Warehouse Operations Uniform
description:
Stratum supplies warehouse and logistics operations across GLMZ's distribution network, and their standard warehouse operations uniform is the daily reality for tens of thousands of workers in the city's fulfillment centers, sorting hubs, and cold-storage facilities. The set consists of a reinforced polo shirt, cargo trousers with articulated knees, a high-visibility safety vest, and an optional thermal liner for cold-chain facilities. The polo and trousers come in company-specific colorways — employers purchase branded versions with their own logo over-printed on the Stratum base — but the cut and construction are standardized. The safety vest is the item with the most technology: embedded in the hi-vis panels are passive RFID nodes that interface with warehouse management systems, logging worker location, task completion, and equipment interaction without requiring active input.

The trousers feature a full tool-loop array at the thigh and hip, sized for handheld scanners, stylus tools, and packing materials. Knee panels are reinforced with gel-core impact absorption for workers who spend time crouching at lower rack levels. Augment compatibility is handled through a universal port-access panel system on the forearms and a back panel with breakaway seams for dorsal chrome. Geneware tail accommodations are standard on all Stratum trousers. Workers generally receive two sets per year and are responsible for their own maintenance — a point of ongoing friction in Stratum-supplied workplaces, as the sets degrade faster than the replacement cycle accounts for.
cultural_context: Stratum warehouse uniforms are one of the most common work garments in GLMZ's lower tiers. The embedded RFID tracking is widely known among workers and widely resented — break-room conversations about the surveillance nodes are a constant undercurrent of warehouse culture. Some workers have developed low-tech methods for briefly masking their vest signals during unauthorized breaks, a practice that has become a minor subculture of its own.
story_hooks: The RFID logs from a Stratum vest place a worker at the scene of a warehouse theft they claim they didn't commit — but the logs have been edited.
A character needs to access a restricted distribution hub; Stratum uniforms are the entry vector, but the RFID nodes will need to be dealt with.
A labor organizer is documenting the gap between Stratum's replacement cycle and actual uniform lifespan as part of a broader wage-theft case.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian and standardized — a crisp polo shirt tucked into cargo trousers, cinched at the waist with a structured belt. The high-visibility safety vest worn over top dominates the silhouette: neon yellow and reflective silver panels create a geometric grid pattern across the torso. The overall impression is deliberately functional and unmistakable — designed to be seen and catalogued in crowded warehouse spaces.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders and chest for mobility, with tapered cargo trousers that taper slightly at the ankle. The vest sits loose over the shirt to accommodate layering and armored undergarments. Articulated knee panels create subtle internal structure. All seams are reinforced and slightly proud of the surface.
physical_description.primary_material: Polo and trousers: poly-blend synth-wool with ballistic weave reinforcement at high-wear points. Safety vest: bonded reflective composite with integrated microfiber backing. Thermal liner (when included): synthetic insulation rated for sub-zero cold-chain work.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and slightly stiff from factory treatment — the poly-blend has a slight sheen under warehouse lighting. Reinforced panels have a subtle quilted texture. The reflective vest panels have a granular, almost sandy feel to touch. All materials are designed to be washable and resistant to chemical degradation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Polo and trousers in company-specific overprinted colorways (usually dark navy, charcoal, or black base with employer logos in secondary colors). Safety vest: International Standard neon yellow-green (Φ#FFF900) with retroreflective silver-white striping in horizontal bands and perpendicular chest cross.
physical_description.closures: Polo: standard buttons down the front. Trousers: friction-fit waistband with integrated loop system and magnetic snap fly closure. Vest: adhesive-backed velcro panels for adjustment, friction-fit armholes. All closures rated for repeated opening/closing over extended shifts.
distinctive_features: Embedded passive RFID nodes in hi-vis panels (location tracking, task logging, equipment interaction)
Full tool-loop array at thigh and hip sized for handheld scanners, styluses, packing materials
Gel-core impact-absorption knee panels for extended crouching work
Universal port-access panels on forearms for augment compatibility
Breakaway seams on back panel for dorsal chrome accommodations
Geneware tail accommodation gussets on all trousers
Company logo over-print on polo chest and trouser hip (employer-specific branding)
Reflective piping along cargo pocket edges for low-light warehouse work
Numbered inventory tag sewn into interior neck label
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 working class — affordable uniform issue for distributed warehouse labor, mass-produced and standardized across GLMZ's logistics network. The embedded RFID technology signals corporate surveillance infrastructure available only to tier 1-2 employers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Daily reality for tens of thousands of fulfillment center, sorting hub, and cold-storage workers. Wearing Stratum signifies you are part of GLMZ's logistics backbone — essential, visible, and monitored. The uniform is a badge of working-class utility and a symbol of workplace surveillance. Subcultures have developed around defeating or masking the RFID nodes during unauthorized breaks, creating a minor but persistent counter-narrative within warehouse culture.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and broken-in after first few shifts. Collar fraying at edges, minor discoloration at forearms and thighs from constant tool contact and dust accumulation. Reflective panels gradually dulling after repeated washings. Seams stressed at underarms and knees. After six months of standard use, visible staining, minor tears, and faded branding. Two sets per year replacement cycle means workers typically operate in compromised condition for the final months before issue.
